metaDescription: Why MessMate exists, how it is built, and the developer behind it.
title: The story behind <accent>MessMate</accent>
subtitle: MessMate is a free app for shared bachelor messes in Bangladesh. It keeps meals, bazaar, bills and deposits in one ledger that every member can see, so the month ends with a bill everyone trusts.

problem.title: The problem
problem.body: In a mess, everyone eats a different number of meals, takes turns at the bazaar and splits rent and bills. Doing the month-end maths by hand takes hours, and someone always finds a mistake.

solution.title: What MessMate does
solution.body: Managers record meals and approve bazaar receipts; members see the meal rate, their bill and their balance at any time. Closing the month produces every final bill and carries balances forward automatically.

stack.title: How it is built
stack.body: A Turborepo monorepo: Next.js 16 and React 19 on the front, a NestJS 11 API, PostgreSQL on Neon with Prisma, and shared Zod schemas so both sides agree on every request.

me.heading: About me
me.bio: I'm a full-stack web developer who loves building modern web applications with Next.js, TypeScript, NestJS, PostgreSQL and Prisma. I worked as a Full Stack Developer Intern at Rise Together (Feb – Jun 2026) on production apps with authentication, payments, real-time features and caching.
me.why: I live in a bachelor mess myself. MessMate started as a way to stop our monthly arguments over the numbers, and grew into the app my whole mess now runs on.
